findings.claim: `disk_headroom_ok` deliberately raises `RuntimeError` when `shutil.disk_usage(home)` itself cannot run (line ~356 doc: "a headroom check that could not run is not a headroom check that passed"), but `check_readiness` calls it unguarded at line 438 with no try/except, so that `RuntimeError` propagates straight out of `check_readiness` instead of becoming a `Readiness(False, "disk", ...)`. Every other step in this function (mirror, origin, default_branch, policy) converts its exception into a named `Readiness` result, and `Readiness`'s own docstring says the whole point is "so a caller can skip the repo and say why ... instead of discovering the reason by reading a traceback the first cell raised" — but for a disk check that cannot execute (permission error, unmounted filesystem, a transient stat failure on `home`), that is exactly what happens: a raw traceback instead of a named skip reason. No test exercises this path through `check_readiness` (the existing test only calls `disk_headroom_ok` directly), so the inconsistency is invisible to the suite.

`check_readiness` wraps every other step's failure mode in try/except and converts it to a named `Readiness(False, step, detail)` (mirror at 407-410, origin at 412-416, default_branch at 418-421, policy at 428-436), but the disk step at line 438 calls `disk_headroom_ok(home)` unguarded. `disk_headroom_ok` deliberately raises `RuntimeError` rather than returning a value when it 'cannot execute' (line 338-344, matching `host_probe_ports`'s precedent), so that RuntimeError propagates straight out of `check_readiness` uncaught. This breaks the function's own documented contract — the `Readiness` dataclass docstring (line 369-371) says the whole point is 'a caller can skip the repo and say why... instead of discovering the reason by reading a traceback' — and it is the one path through the single entry point where a caller still gets exactly that traceback, for the same 'cannot execute' class of failure every sibling check converts into a named result.

`validate_claude_token`'s actual pass/fail determination — `exc.code not in (401, 403)` on an `HTTPError`, and the bare `return True` on success — is never exercised by any test. `test_the_token_probes_default_request_shape_is_asserted_not_sent` only makes `urlopen` raise `URLError`, which takes the separate `except urllib.error.URLError: return False` branch; no test anywhere constructs an `HTTPError`. Every other test that exercises `check_readiness`'s auth step injects a fake `validate_token` callable and never calls the real function at all. Changing line 315 to `return True` (treat any HTTPError, including 401/403, as a valid token) keeps every test in the suite green while silently reinstating exactly the Appendix J landmine this spec exists to close — an expired token would again pass readiness.

except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        return exc.code not in (401, 403)
